page: Client Components in hono/jsx/dom for browser-side interactive UI. hono/jsx/dom is lightweight: 2.8KB with Brotli compression vs React 47.8KB. Imports: useState, render from hono/jsx/dom. React hooks available: useState, useEffect, useRef, useCallback, use, startTransition, useTransition, useDeferredValue, useMemo, useLayoutEffect, useReducer, useDebugValue, createElement, memo, isValidElement, useId, createRef, forwardRef, useImperativeHandle, useSyncExternalStore, useInsertionEffect, useFormStatus, useActionState, useOptimistic. View Transitions API support via startViewTransition, viewTransition, useViewTransition hooks. Configuration: tsconfig.json jsxImportSource hono/jsx/dom, Vite esbuild option jsxImportSource. Example: Counter component with render() into element. Questions: How do I create interactive components in Hono? How small is hono/jsx/dom? Which React hooks are supported? How do I configure View Transitions? What's the render function syntax?

sections.manifest: Counter component example using hono/jsx/dom. Imports: useState from hono/jsx, render from hono/jsx/dom. Component structure: Counter component with useState(0), increment button onClick, App component wrapping Counter, render(<App />, document.getElementById('root')). Demonstrates basic interactive UI pattern. Reference: Counter example at github.com/honojs/examples/tree/main/hono-vite-jsx. Questions: How do I build a counter? What's the basic component structure? How do I use onClick handlers?

render() function inserts JSX components into DOM elements. Syntax: render(<Component />, container). Parameter 1: JSX component. Parameter 2: target HTML element or container node. Returns rendered component instance. Usage: after DOM is ready. Enables dynamic UI injection into existing HTML. Questions: How do I render components to the DOM? What parameters does render take? Can I render multiple components?

React-compatible hooks in hono/jsx/dom. State/Effect: useState, useEffect, useRef, useReducer, useLayoutEffect, useInsertionEffect. Callback/Async: useCallback, useTransition, startTransition, useDeferredValue, useMemo. Component: createElement, memo, isValidElement, useId, createRef, forwardRef, useImperativeHandle. External: useSyncExternalStore. Form: useFormStatus, useActionState, useOptimistic. All hooks work same as React; documentation available at react.dev/reference/react/hooks. Questions: Which React hooks are available? Do hooks work the same as React? Where do I find hook documentation?

View Transitions API support via three patterns. startViewTransition(): wraps document.startViewTransition, callback-based. Example: startViewTransition(() => setShowLargeImage(!showLargeImage)). viewTransition(): returns unique view-transition-name, used with keyframes() and ::view-transition-old/new pseudo-elements. Syntax: viewTransition(css`...`)). useViewTransition(): hook returning [isUpdating, startViewTransition()], component re-evaluates during animation and when finish promise fulfills. Used for conditional styles during transition. Requires css, keyframes, Style from hono/css. Questions: How do I add View Transitions? How do I customize transition animations? How do I detect when transition is active?

hono/jsx/dom runtime configuration for smaller bundles than hono/jsx. tsconfig.json: jsx: "react-jsx", jsxImportSource: "hono/jsx/dom". Deno: modify deno.json same way. Vite alternative: esbuild option jsxImportSource: "hono/jsx/dom" in vite.config.ts. Trade-off: smaller package, full React hook compatibility. Questions: How do I configure hono/jsx/dom? What's the tsconfig syntax? How do I set up Vite for hono/jsx/dom?
